The Guardian reports that public bodies spent £3.4 billion on private consultants in the past year, a 62% increase compared to 2019-20, according to data from Tussell. Despite expectations that spending would decrease after the pandemic, it remains elevated. This poses a significant issue for the new administration, which plans to reduce consultant expenditures by half during its term.

Recent contracts include a £223 million agreement with KPMG to train civil servants, part of nearly £650 million in new deals awarded since the recent change in leadership. Critics, like Labour peer Prem Sikka, argue that relying on consultants is excessive, questioning their ability to deliver meaningful insights in short periods.

Is there anything else I can help with?
